To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the metanephros develops from two primordia, the ureteric bud and the metanephronic mesenchyme; (ii) the metanephronephric mesenchyme contains a subpopulation of cells that are capable of differentiating into tubule cells; (iii) the differentiation process is initiated by the ureteric buds; (iv) differentiation of the metaneplrogenic mesenchymes involves a stimulation of DNA synthesis; and (

(a) determination of the mesenchymal cells starts around 24 hr after explantation; and (b) the stimulation of DNA synthesis is a permissive effect that is necessary for the differentiation of the metenephrogenic mesen-chyme.
the metanephron is formed by a metanephrogenesis process that is initiated when the mesenchyme is stimulated by a contact-mediated interaction between the metanephros and the inductor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction and control of the formation of the kidney in the developing embryo.
the molecular mechanisms of cell-cell interactions.
the mechanisms involved in the differentiation of the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
induction is not a prerequisite for DNA synthesis but that DNA synthesis is a prerequisite for induction.

the mesenchyme has the potential of differentiating in vitro into epithelial cells and that the spinal cord is the inductor of this process, and that the induction is mediated through the contact between the inductor and the target cells.

induction of the mesenchyme is not accompanied by an increase in cell proliferation but rather that induction is accompanied by a stimulation of DNA synthesis in the target cells, and that this stimulation may be a permissive event for the differentiation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

induction is a two-step process: (a) determination, which is completed in 24 hr and is accompanied by an increase in DNA synthesis, and (b) differentiation, which is initiated by the inductor and proceeds in a contact-mediated manner.
determination of the mesenchyme starts at 12-14 hr and is completed at 24 hr; differentiation is induced at 24 hr, but does not start until 48 hr.
the determination process is completed within 12 hr and differentiation is initiated at 24 hr after setting up transfilter cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mesenchyme is not a homogeneous cell population.
induction of metanephric differentiation is accompanied by a stimulation of DNA synthesis.

the mesenchymal cell cycle is extended during the determination phase and that the determination phase can be interrupted by a brief exposure of the mesenchyme to a noninducing tissue or to a noninductive medium.
